# MyGround

> MyGround is a free, MIT-licensed self-hosting platform: one Rust binary with an embedded web UI that installs and runs self-hosted apps in Docker on your own Linux (x86_64, ARM64) or macOS machine, with automatic backups, health checks and updates for each app. It replaces Google Photos, Netflix, Spotify, Google Drive and similar cloud services with apps you own.

The catalog has 31 curated apps with one-click install, including Immich (photos), Jellyfin (media), Navidrome (music), Nextcloud (files, contacts, calendar), Vaultwarden (passwords), Pi-hole (DNS ad blocking), Audiobookshelf, Kavita, Home Assistant, Gitea, Firefly III, Mealie, Open WebUI and Ollama. Backups use restic to S3, Backblaze B2, Wasabi or local disk, with per-app schedules, database dumps, snapshot browsing and one-click restore. NVIDIA and Intel GPUs can be passed through to Immich and Jellyfin. Every app can get its own Tailscale node with automatic HTTPS, or be exposed through a Cloudflare Tunnel; any app's traffic can go through a Gluetun VPN. Everything in the web UI is also in the CLI and a REST API with an OpenAPI spec and API keys, so AI agents can manage the server.

Install: `curl -fsSL https://myground.online/install.sh | sh` (installs Docker if needed and sets up a systemd service), or `brew install backmeupplz/myground/myground`, `apt install myground`, `yay -S myground`.
